bioprojects.title: Trypanosoma cruzi strain Esmeraldo genome sequencing
NHGRI Large Scale Sequencing Program for Organismal Sequencing

assembly_info.comments:
Background: The Trypanosome cruzi Esmeraldo strain cl3 was obtained from Dr. Gregory Buck, Center for the Study of Biological Complexity, Microbiology and Immunology, Virginia Commonwealth University. This strain, a representative of the TcIIb lineage, was isolated from a male patient,
20 years old, in acute phase of the Chagas disease patient in Sao Felipe, Bahia State, Brazil, by Dr. Michael A. Miles(Miles et al., 1977). A clonal derivative was prepared in the laboratory of Dr. Michael A. Miles at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and used for sequencing. Genomic DNA was prepared by Andrey Matveyev at Virginia Commonwealth University. Total genomic DNA was depleted for kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA (kDNA), which represents up to 30-50% of the total DNA in the cell. In brief, total DNA was carefully extracted from cultured late log phase T. cruzi Esmeraldo strain epimastigote forms and submitted to low voltage electrophoresis in 0.8% low melting agarose. The gDNA-containing agarose blocks were excised from the gel, leaving the kDNA networks intact in the gel. Purified gDNA was recovered from the agarose blocks after digestion using Beta-agarase I.
Next-generation sequences on the 454 instruments were produced for a draft assembly. Total sequence coverage of 454 instrument reads was
63X (Fragments 47X, 3Kb PE 11X, 8Kb PE 5X) using a genome size estimate of 40Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the Newbler software (Roche 454). This first draft assembly was referred to as T_cruzi_Esmeraldo_5.1.3. This version has been cleaned of contaminants. The assembly is made up of a total of 15,803 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 58kb (N50 contig length for the 26,998 contigs was 5.3kb). The assembly spans 34.9Mb. This assembly is subject to change due to ongoing assembly improvement efforts.
This work was supported by NSF DEB-0830056 grant to Gregory Buck and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.
For questions regarding this T_cruzi_Esmeraldo_5.1.3 assembly please contact Dr. Wes Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@watson.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Trypanosoma cruzi Esmeraldo strain cI3 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Any publications that propose to use whole genome or chromosome data should contact The Genome Institute at Washington University (gweinsto@wustl.edu or wwarren@wustl.edu) for the use of pre-publication data.
